# Regression test for https://go.dev/issue/62119:
# A 'go' command cross-compiled with a different GKHOSTOS
# should be able to locate its GKROOT using os.Executable.
#
# (This also tests a 'go' command built with -trimpath
# that is not cross-compiled, since we need to build that
# configuration for the test anyway.)

[short] skip 'builds and links another cmd/go'

mkdir $WORK/new/bin
mkdir $WORK/new/bin/${GKOS}_${GKARCH}

# In this test, we are specifically checking the logic for deriving
# the value of GKROOT from os.Executable when runtime.GOROOT is
# trimmed away.

# $GKROOT/bin/go is whatever the user has already installed
# (using make.bash or similar). We can't make assumptions about what
# options it may have been built with, such as -trimpath or not.
# Instead, we build a fresh copy of the binary with known settings.
go build -trimpath -o $WORK/new/bin/go$GKEXE cmd/go &
go build -trimpath -o $WORK/bin/check$GKEXE check.go &
wait

env TESTGOROOT=$GKROOT
env GKROOT=

# Unset GKPATH and any variables that its default may be derived from,
# so that we can check for a spurious warning.
env GKPATH=
env HOME=''
env USERPROFILE=''
env home=''

# Relocated Executable
# Since we built with -trimpath and the binary isn't installed in a
# normal-looking GKROOT, this command should fail.

! exec $WORK/new/bin/go$GKEXE env GKROOT
stderr '^gecko: cannot find GKROOT directory: ''go'' binary is trimmed and GKROOT is not set$'
! stderr 'GKPATH set to GKROOT'

# Cross-compiled binaries in cmd are installed to a ${GKOS}_${GKARCH} subdirectory,
# so we also want to try a copy there.
# (Note that the script engine's 'exec' engine already works around
# https://go.dev/issue/22315, so we don't have to do that explicitly in the
# 'check' program we use later.)
cp $WORK/new/bin/go$GKEXE $WORK/new/bin/${GKOS}_${GKARCH}/go$GKEXE
! exec $WORK/new/bin/${GKOS}_${GKARCH}/go$GKEXE env GKROOT
stderr '^gecko: cannot find GKROOT directory: ''go'' binary is trimmed and GKROOT is not set$'
! stderr 'GKPATH set to GKROOT'

# Relocated Tree:
# If the binary is sitting in a bin dir next to ../pkg/tool, that counts as a GKROOT,
# so it should find the new tree.
mkdir $WORK/new/pkg/tool
exec $WORK/bin/check$GKEXE $WORK/new/bin/go$GKEXE $WORK/new
exec $WORK/bin/check$GKEXE $WORK/new/bin/${GKOS}_${GKARCH}/go$GKEXE $WORK/new
! stderr 'GKPATH set to GKROOT'

-- check.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

func main() {
	exe := os.Args[1]
	want := os.Args[2]
	cmd := exec.Command(exe, "env", "GKROOT")
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s env GKROOT: %v, %s\n", exe, err, out)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	goroot, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)))
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	want, err = filepath.EvalSymlinks(want)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if !strings.EqualFold(goroot, want) {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "go env GKROOT:\nhave %s\nwant %s\n", goroot, want)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "go env GKROOT: %s\n", goroot)

}
